CompositorNodeAlphaOver.node: Lays a foreground image on top of a background, using the foreground's transparency, like stacking a sticker on a photo.

inputs.Background: The bottom picture, seen wherever the foreground is see-through.
inputs.Foreground: The top picture, placed over the background. Its transparent parts let the background show.
inputs.Fac: How strongly the foreground is laid on. 0 shows only the background, 1 shows the full overlay.
inputs.Type: Chooses how the two images are mixed. Convert Premultiplied handles images whose colors were already multiplied by their transparency.
inputs.Straight Alpha: Turn on if the foreground has straight (unpremultiplied) alpha. Wrong setting causes dark or bright halos at edges.

CompositorNodeAntiAliasing.node: Smooths jagged, stair-step edges in an image, Use it on renders with hard edges.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Threshold: How big a color jump must be to count as an edge. Low smooths more edges, high only the sharpest ones.
inputs.Contrast Limit: Limits how much weaker nearby edges can be before they are ignored. Low smooths more, high keeps fine detail.
inputs.Corner Rounding: How much sharp corners get rounded. 0 keeps corners crisp, higher values soften them.

CompositorNodeBilateralblur.node: Blurs an image but tries to keep edges sharp, like smoothing skin without blurring the outline of a face.

inputs.Image: The picture to blur.
inputs.Determinator: A guide image that tells the blur where the edges are. Often the same picture, or a normal or depth pass.
inputs.Size: How far the blur reaches, in pixels. Low is a light smoothing, high is a strong smoothing.
inputs.Threshold: How different two colors must be to stop the blur. Low protects more edges, high blurs across more of them.

CompositorNodeBlankImage.node: Makes a flat, single-color image of a chosen size. Use it as a plain background or a starting canvas.

inputs.Color: The color that fills the whole image.
inputs.Size: Width and height of the new image in pixels. Bigger numbers make a larger image.

CompositorNodeBlur.node: Softens an image by mixing each pixel with its neighbors, like frosted glass.

inputs.Image: The picture to blur.
inputs.Size: How far the blur spreads sideways (X) and up and down (Y). Low is slightly soft, high is very smeared.
inputs.Type: The blur style. Different types trade speed for look, such as Gaussian for natural softness or Box for a blocky blur.
inputs.Extend Bounds: If on, the blur may spread past the image edges so the borders fade out instead of staying sharp.
inputs.Separable: If on, blurs sideways and up and down separately. Faster, but only on blur types where this gives the same look.

CompositorNodeBokehBlur.node: Blurs an image using a custom shape, like the soft bright discs of an out-of-focus camera lens.

inputs.Image: The picture to blur.
inputs.Bokeh: A small image whose shape becomes the look of the blur, such as a circle or hexagon. Make one with Bokeh Image.
inputs.Size: How strong the blur is. Low is slight, high is very out of focus.
inputs.Mask: A gray map that picks where to blur. White areas are blurred fully, black areas stay sharp.
inputs.Extend Bounds: If on, the blur may spread past the image edges so borders fade out naturally.

CompositorNodeBokehImage.node: Draws the shape of a camera lens opening, like a hexagon. Feed it into Bokeh Blur to shape the blur.

inputs.Flaps: How many sides the shape has, like the blades of a camera iris. 3 is a triangle, higher gets rounder.
inputs.Angle: Turns the shape around its center, like rotating a hexagon.
inputs.Roundness: Blends from sharp straight sides (0) to a perfect circle (1).
inputs.Catadioptric Size: Cuts a hole in the middle like a mirror lens (donut look). 0 is solid, higher makes a bigger hole.
inputs.Color Shift: Adds color fringes to the shape edges. 0 is none, higher gives stronger rainbow edges.

CompositorNodeBoxMask.node: Draws a white rectangle on black. Use it as a mask to show or hide part of an image, like a window cut in paper.

inputs.Operation: How this mask joins the one plugged into Mask. Add combines them, Subtract cuts it out, Multiply keeps the overlap, Not inverts.
inputs.Mask: An existing mask to combine with this shape. If nothing is connected, it starts from black (empty).
inputs.Value: How bright the shape is. 1 is full white, lower values make a softer, see-through shape.
inputs.Position: Where the center of the box sits. 0 to 1 across the image, so 0.5 is the middle.
inputs.Size: Width and height of the box as part of the image. 1 fills the whole image.
inputs.Rotation: Turns the box in degrees around its center.

CompositorNodeBrightContrast.node: Makes an image lighter or darker and adjusts how different bright and dark areas are, like a simple photo editor.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Bright: Adds or removes light. Negative makes it darker, 0 is no change, positive makes it brighter.
inputs.Contrast: Pushes light and dark further apart. Negative looks flat and gray, positive looks punchy.

CompositorNodeChannelMatte.node: Cuts out parts of an image by comparing one color channel to others, like removing a green screen by its green amount.

inputs.Image: The picture to cut a background from.
inputs.Minimum: Below this key strength, pixels become fully transparent. Raise it to cut out more.
inputs.Maximum: Above this key strength, pixels stay fully solid. The range between Minimum and Maximum is a soft fade.
inputs.Color Space: The color system used for the test: RGB, HSV, YUV or YCbCr. Pick the one that separates your key color best.
inputs.RGB Key Channel: Which of Red, Green or Blue is the color you want to remove, such as Green for a green screen.
inputs.HSV Key Channel: Which of Hue, Saturation or Value is the part used to find the background.
inputs.YUV Key Channel: Which YUV channel is used to find the background (Y is brightness, U and V are color).
inputs.YCbCr Key Channel: Which YCbCr channel is used to find the background (Y is brightness, Cb and Cr are color).
inputs.Limit Method: How the key strength is limited. Single compares to the strongest other channel, Max to the brightest of the rest.
inputs.RGB Limit Channel: Which RGB channel the key is compared against. Pick the one that tends to be higher than the key in your background.
inputs.HSV Limit Channel: Which HSV channel the key is compared against when limiting.
inputs.YUV Limit Channel: Which YUV channel the key is compared against when limiting.
inputs.YCbCr Limit Channel: Which YCbCr channel the key is compared against when limiting.

CompositorNodeChromaMatte.node: Removes a chosen color (like green screen) from an image and makes it transparent, so you can place a subject on a new background.

inputs.Image: The footage with the colored backdrop.
inputs.Key Color: The color to remove, such as the green of your screen. Use the eyedropper for best results.
inputs.Minimum: Angle of color difference that is fully removed. Higher removes more shades near the key color.
inputs.Maximum: Angle of color difference past which pixels are fully kept. Larger gap with Minimum gives a softer edge.
inputs.Falloff: How softly the edge fades between removed and kept. 0 is hard-edged, higher is smoother.

CompositorNodeColorBalance.node: Tints an image's dark, mid and bright areas separately, like the color grading in a movie. Use it to set a mood.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Fac: How strongly the effect is applied. 0 leaves the image alone, 1 is full effect.
inputs.Type: Chooses the method: Lift/Gamma/Gain, Offset/Power/Slope (ASC CDL), or White Point (temperature and tint).
inputs.Base Lift: Brightens or darkens the shadows without changing the highlights much.
inputs.Color Lift: Tints the shadows (dark areas) toward a color.
inputs.Base Gamma: Makes the mid-tones lighter or darker. Below 1 darker, above 1 brighter.
inputs.Color Gamma: Tints the mid-tones toward a color.
inputs.Base Gain: Scales the highlights (bright areas). Low dims them, high makes them brighter.
inputs.Color Gain: Tints the highlights (bright areas) toward a color.
inputs.Base Offset: Adds or subtracts the same amount from every pixel. Negative makes it darker, positive lifts it all.
inputs.Color Offset: Adds a color tint to the whole picture evenly.
inputs.Base Power: Bends the mid-tones like gamma. Higher values make the picture darker in the middle.
inputs.Color Power: Tints the mid-tones by color, using the power curve.
inputs.Base Slope: Scales overall brightness, strongest on bright areas. Low is dimmer, high is brighter.
inputs.Color Slope: Tints bright areas toward a color, using the slope control.
inputs.Input Temperature: How warm or cool the original lighting looks, so it can be neutralized. Low is cool blue, high is warm orange.
inputs.Input Tint: Green or magenta lean of the original lighting, so it can be neutralized.
inputs.Output Temperature: The warmth you want the final picture to have. Low is cool blue, high is warm orange.
inputs.Output Tint: The green or magenta lean you want in the final picture.

CompositorNodeColorCorrection.node: Adjusts saturation, contrast, gamma, gain and offset separately for shadows, midtones and highlights. A full color grading toolbox.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Mask: A gray map choosing where the correction shows. White applies it fully, black leaves the image untouched.
inputs.Master Saturation: Color strength of the whole image. 0 is gray, 1 is unchanged, higher is more vivid.
inputs.Master Contrast: Contrast of the whole image. Below 1 looks flatter, above 1 pushes light and dark apart.
inputs.Master Gamma: Brightness of the mid-values within the whole image. Below 1 is brighter, above 1 darker.
inputs.Master Gain: Multiplies the brightness of the whole image. Low dims, high brightens.
inputs.Master Offset: Adds or subtracts light evenly from the whole image. Negative darkens, positive lightens.
inputs.Highlights Saturation: Color strength of the bright areas. 0 is gray, 1 is unchanged, higher is more vivid.
inputs.Highlights Contrast: Contrast of the bright areas. Below 1 looks flatter, above 1 pushes light and dark apart.
inputs.Highlights Gamma: Brightness of the mid-values within the bright areas. Below 1 is brighter, above 1 darker.
inputs.Highlights Gain: Multiplies the brightness of the bright areas. Low dims, high brightens.
inputs.Highlights Offset: Adds or subtracts light evenly from the bright areas. Negative darkens, positive lightens.
inputs.Midtones Saturation: Color strength of the middle brightness areas. 0 is gray, 1 is unchanged, higher is more vivid.
inputs.Midtones Contrast: Contrast of the middle brightness areas. Below 1 looks flatter, above 1 pushes light and dark apart.
inputs.Midtones Gamma: Brightness of the mid-values within the middle brightness areas. Below 1 is brighter, above 1 darker.
inputs.Midtones Gain: Multiplies the brightness of the middle brightness areas. Low dims, high brightens.
inputs.Midtones Offset: Adds or subtracts light evenly from the middle brightness areas. Negative darkens, positive lightens.
inputs.Shadows Saturation: Color strength of the dark areas. 0 is gray, 1 is unchanged, higher is more vivid.
inputs.Shadows Contrast: Contrast of the dark areas. Below 1 looks flatter, above 1 pushes light and dark apart.
inputs.Shadows Gamma: Brightness of the mid-values within the dark areas. Below 1 is brighter, above 1 darker.
inputs.Shadows Gain: Multiplies the brightness of the dark areas. Low dims, high brightens.
inputs.Shadows Offset: Adds or subtracts light evenly from the dark areas. Negative darkens, positive lightens.
inputs.Midtones Start: Brightness where shadows end and midtones begin. Raising it widens the shadow range.
inputs.Midtones End: Brightness where midtones end and highlights begin. Lowering it widens the highlight range.
inputs.Apply On Red: If on, the correction changes the red channel. Turn off to leave red untouched.
inputs.Apply On Green: If on, the correction changes the green channel. Turn off to leave green untouched.
inputs.Apply On Blue: If on, the correction changes the blue channel. Turn off to leave blue untouched.

CompositorNodeColorMatte.node: Makes pixels close to a chosen color transparent, based on hue, saturation and value. Good for removing a solid-color backdrop.

inputs.Image: The picture with a colored backdrop.
inputs.Key Color: The color you want to remove.
inputs.Hue: How far the hue (the color itself) may differ from the key and still be removed. Higher removes more shades.
inputs.Saturation: How far color strength may differ from the key and still be removed. Higher removes more pale or vivid versions.
inputs.Value: How far brightness may differ from the key and still be removed. Higher removes more lighter or darker versions.

CompositorNodeColorSpill.node: Removes the leftover tint of a green or blue screen that bounced onto your subject, like cleaning green light off a person's hair.

inputs.Image: The keyed picture that has a color cast on its edges.
inputs.Fac: How much of the spill is removed. 0 does nothing, 1 removes as much as the settings allow.
inputs.Spill Channel: The color channel (Red, Green or Blue) that is spilling. Choose the color of your screen.
inputs.Limit Method: How the spill is measured. Single compares to one other channel, Average to the mix of the other two.
inputs.Limit Channel: Which other channel the spill is compared to when Limit Method is Single.
inputs.Limit Strength: How much the limiting channel counts. Higher removes less spill, lower removes more.
inputs.Use Spill Strength: If on, you can set a separate removal strength for each color channel with Strength.
inputs.Spill Strength: Per-channel amount of spill removed (red, green, blue). Only used if Use Spill Strength is on.

CompositorNodeCombineColor.node: Builds a color image from separate red, green, blue and alpha numbers or images. The reverse of Separate Color.

inputs.Red: The red amount for each pixel. 0 is none, 1 is full red.
inputs.Green: The green amount for each pixel. 0 is none, 1 is full green.
inputs.Blue: The blue amount for each pixel. 0 is none, 1 is full blue.
inputs.Alpha: How solid each pixel is. 0 is invisible, 1 is fully visible.

CompositorNodeConvertColorSpace.node: Changes the color system of an image from one to another, so colors look right when used somewhere else.

inputs.Image: The picture whose color system will be converted.

CompositorNodeConvertToDisplay.node: Changes an image so it looks the same as on your screen, with the view and look settings baked in. Use before saving a display-ready image.

inputs.Image: The picture to convert for display.
inputs.Invert: If on, does the reverse: turns display-ready colors back into scene colors.

CompositorNodeConvolve.node: Applies a custom filter shape to an image by blending each pixel using a small pattern, which can blur, sharpen or create glows.

inputs.Image: The picture to filter.
inputs.Kernel Data Type: Whether the filter pattern is a gray-only map (Float) or has color (Color).
inputs.Float Kernel: A gray image used as the pattern. Bright spots decide how pixels are spread around.
inputs.Color Kernel: A color image used as the pattern. Its colors and shapes are stamped across the picture.
inputs.Normalize Kernel: If on, scales the pattern so brightness stays the same. Turn off and the picture may get much brighter.

CompositorNodeCornerPin.node: Squeezes and stretches an image into any four-cornered shape, like pinning a poster onto a wall in perspective.

inputs.Image: The picture to reshape.
inputs.Upper Left: Where the top-left corner of the image lands. Move it to bend the picture.
inputs.Upper Right: Where the top-right corner of the image lands.
inputs.Lower Left: Where the bottom-left corner of the image lands.
inputs.Lower Right: Where the bottom-right corner of the image lands.
inputs.Interpolation: How pixels are blended when moved or resampled. Nearest is crisp and blocky, Bilinear and Bicubic are smoother.
inputs.Extension X: What fills space past the left and right edges. Clip leaves it empty, Extend stretches the edge pixels, Repeat tiles the image.
inputs.Extension Y: What fills space past the top and bottom edges. Clip leaves it empty, Extend stretches the edge pixels, Repeat tiles the image.

CompositorNodeCrop.node: Cuts away the edges of an image, keeping only a rectangle. Use it to trim a picture or focus on one part.

inputs.Image: The picture to crop.
inputs.X: Left edge of the crop box, in pixels from the left. Higher cuts more from the left side.
inputs.Y: Bottom edge of the crop box, in pixels from the bottom. Higher cuts more from the bottom.
inputs.Width: Width of the crop box in pixels. Smaller keeps a narrower piece.
inputs.Height: Height of the crop box in pixels. Smaller keeps a shorter piece.
inputs.Alpha Crop: If on, the cropped-away area becomes transparent and the image keeps its size. If off, the image gets smaller.

CompositorNodeCryptomatte.node: Older tool that picks objects or materials out of a render using special ID passes, to make masks without extra renders.

inputs.Image: The regular picture to show with the picked parts.
inputs.Crypto 00: First Cryptomatte data layer from your render. Connect the matching pass.
inputs.Crypto 01: Second Cryptomatte data layer from your render.
inputs.Crypto 02: Third Cryptomatte data layer from your render.

CompositorNodeCryptomatteV2.node: Picks objects, materials or assets out of a render to make clean masks, by clicking their names. No extra rendering needed.

inputs.Image: The regular picture shown with the picked parts removed or kept.

CompositorNodeCurveRGB.node: Reshapes brightness and color with drawn curves, like the curves tool in a photo editor. Great for contrast and color tweaks.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Fac: How strongly the curves are applied. 0 leaves the image unchanged, 1 is full effect.
inputs.Black Level: The color that counts as pure black. Pixels at this color become black. Raising it deepens the shadows.
inputs.White Level: The color that counts as pure white. Pixels at this color become white. Lowering it brightens the picture.

CompositorNodeDBlur.node: Smears an image in a direction, spinning, or zooming, like motion lines from a fast camera move.

inputs.Image: The picture to smear.
inputs.Samples: How many copies are blended. Low is choppy and fast, high is smooth and slower.
inputs.Center: The middle point for the spin and zoom smear. 0.5 is the image center.
inputs.Rotation: How much the smear spins around the center, in degrees. 0 is none.
inputs.Scale: How much the smear zooms in or out from the center. 0 is none, higher streaks outward.
inputs.Translation Amount: How far the smear slides, as part of the image size. 0 is none, higher is a longer streak.
inputs.Translation Direction: The angle that the slide smear points in, in degrees.

CompositorNodeDefocus.node: Blurs an image based on a depth map, so things far from focus look soft like a camera with shallow depth of field.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Z: A depth map that says how far each pixel is. Without it, the blur is the same everywhere.

CompositorNodeDenoise.node: Removes grain and speckles (noise) from a rendered image using a smart filter, so renders look clean with fewer samples.

inputs.Image: The noisy picture to clean.
inputs.Albedo: Optional pass of pure surface colors. Helps the cleaner keep texture detail.
inputs.Normal: Optional pass of surface directions. Helps the cleaner keep shapes and edges sharp.
inputs.HDR: Turn on for images with very bright values (like renders). Off clamps to normal brightness.
inputs.Prefilter: How the helper passes are cleaned first. None is fastest, Fast is quick, Accurate is slow but best.
inputs.Quality: Speed versus result. High gives the cleanest picture but takes longer, Balanced and Fast take less time.

CompositorNodeDespeckle.node: Removes tiny bright or dark specks from an image, like dust, while leaving larger shapes alone.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Fac: How strongly the cleanup is applied. 0 does nothing, 1 is the full effect.
inputs.Color Threshold: How different a pixel's color must be from neighbors to count as a speck. Low cleans more, high cleans less.
inputs.Neighbor Threshold: How many nearby pixels must differ before it is cleaned. Low cleans more, high only strong specks.

CompositorNodeDiffMatte.node: Makes a pixel transparent if it is nearly the same in two images. Use it to remove a still background by comparing it to a shot without the subject.

inputs.Image 1: The shot with the subject in it.
inputs.Image 2: The clean shot of just the background to compare against.
inputs.Tolerance: How different two pixels may be and still count as the same. Low removes less, high removes more.
inputs.Falloff: How softly the cutout edge fades. 0 is hard, higher gives a smoother, partly see-through edge.

CompositorNodeDilateErode.node: Grows or shrinks the white area of a mask, so a shape gets thicker or thinner. Good for fixing mask edges.

inputs.Mask: The black and white mask to grow or shrink.
inputs.Size: How many pixels to change. Positive grows white areas, negative shrinks them.
inputs.Type: The method used. Steps is a plain grow or shrink, Threshold, Distance and Feather give different edge looks.
inputs.Falloff Size: Width of the soft edge in Feather mode. Larger gives a softer, longer fade.
inputs.Falloff: The shape of the soft edge fade, such as Smooth, Sphere, Root or Sharp.

CompositorNodeDisplace.node: Pushes pixels of an image around using another image as a guide, like distorting a picture seen through rippled glass.

inputs.Image: The picture to distort.
inputs.Displacement: A vector map that says how far to move each pixel in X and Y. Bigger values shift pixels farther.
inputs.Interpolation: How pixels are blended when moved or resampled. Nearest is crisp and blocky, Bilinear and Bicubic are smoother.
inputs.Extension X: What fills space past the left and right edges. Clip leaves it empty, Extend stretches the edge pixels, Repeat tiles the image.
inputs.Extension Y: What fills space past the top and bottom edges. Clip leaves it empty, Extend stretches the edge pixels, Repeat tiles the image.

CompositorNodeDistanceMatte.node: Removes pixels whose color is close to a chosen color. Works like Chroma Key but by simple color distance.

inputs.Image: The picture with a backdrop to remove.
inputs.Color Space: Which color system distance is measured in, RGB or YCC. Pick whichever isolates your color better.
inputs.Tolerance: How close a color must be to the key to be removed. Low removes only near matches, high removes many shades.
inputs.Falloff: How softly the edge fades between removed and kept. 0 is hard, higher is smoother.

CompositorNodeDoubleEdgeMask.node: Builds a soft border between an inner and an outer mask, helpful for blending an object edge in the gap between them.

inputs.Outer Mask: A mask drawn loosely around the outside of the shape.
inputs.Inner Mask: A mask drawn tightly inside the shape. The gap between inner and outer becomes the edge.
inputs.Image Edges: If on, the borders of the image itself also count as edges.
inputs.Only Inside Outer: If on, the edge result is kept only inside the outer mask. Off may leak outside it.

CompositorNodeEllipseMask.node: Draws a white oval on black. Use it as a mask to show or hide part of an image, like a spotlight or a vignette.

inputs.Operation: How this mask joins the one plugged into Mask. Add combines them, Subtract cuts it out, Multiply keeps the overlap, Not inverts.
inputs.Mask: An existing mask to combine with this shape. If nothing is connected, it starts from black (empty).
inputs.Value: How bright the shape is. 1 is full white, lower values make a softer, see-through shape.
inputs.Position: Where the center of the oval sits. 0 to 1 across the image, so 0.5 is the middle.
inputs.Size: Width and height of the oval as part of the image. 1 fills the whole image.
inputs.Rotation: Turns the oval in degrees around its center.

CompositorNodeExposure.node: Brightens or darkens an image like changing camera exposure. Each whole step doubles or halves the light.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Exposure: Camera-style stops of light. 0 is no change, +1 doubles the brightness, -1 halves it.

CompositorNodeFilter.node: Applies a classic image filter such as sharpen, edge detect or emboss, like a quick effect in a photo editor.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Fac: How strongly the filter is applied. 0 leaves the picture as is, 1 is the full effect.
inputs.Type: Which filter to use: Soften, Box Sharpen, Diamond Sharpen, Laplace, Sobel, Prewitt, Kirsch or Shadow.

CompositorNodeFlip.node: Mirrors an image sideways, upside down, or both, like flipping a photo over.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Flip X: If on, flips the image left to right.
inputs.Flip Y: If on, flips the image top to bottom.

CompositorNodeGlare.node: Adds glowing light around bright parts of an image, like bloom, light streaks, stars or a sun beam. Makes lights feel brighter.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Type: The style of glow: Bloom, Ghosts, Streaks, Fog Glow, Simple Star, Sun Beams or Kernel.
inputs.Quality: Speed versus smoothness of the glow. High looks best but is slower, Low is fast but rougher.
inputs.Highlights Threshold: Brightness a pixel must reach to glow. Low makes many things glow, high only the brightest lights.
inputs.Highlights Smoothness: How softly pixels near the threshold fade in. 0 is a hard cut, higher is a gentle start.
inputs.Clamp Highlights: If on, extremely bright pixels are capped at the Maximum value before glowing.
inputs.Maximum Highlights: The brightest value allowed to glow when Clamp is on. Lower stops very bright lights from overpowering.
inputs.Strength: How bright the glow is added back. 0 is none, higher is stronger.
inputs.Saturation: Color strength of the glow. 0 is gray, 1 is normal, higher is more vivid.
inputs.Tint: Colors the glow. White keeps it natural, other colors tint it.
inputs.Size: How far the glow spreads. Low is a tight halo, high is a wide soft cloud.
inputs.Streaks: How many light rays are drawn. More gives a fuller star pattern.
inputs.Streaks Angle: Turns the whole streak pattern, in degrees.
inputs.Iterations: How many times the glow is repeated. More makes streaks longer and ghosts more numerous but slower.
inputs.Fade: How quickly streaks dim along their length. Low fades fast, high lets them run long.
inputs.Color Modulation: How much the repeated glows shift in color. 0 keeps them the same, higher gives rainbow shades.
inputs.Diagonal Star: If on, the simple star also has diagonal rays. Off draws only a plus-shaped star.
inputs.Sun Position: Where the light beams come from, 0 to 1 across the image. 0.5 is the center.
inputs.Jitter: Randomly shifts the rays for a rougher, more natural beam. 0 is smooth.
inputs.Kernel Data Type: Whether the custom glow shape is gray-only (Float) or has color (Color).
inputs.Float Kernel: A gray image whose shape stamps the glow at each bright spot.
inputs.Color Kernel: A color image whose shape and colors stamp the glow at each bright spot.

CompositorNodeHueCorrect.node: Changes the hue, saturation and value of only certain colors using curves, like making blues deeper without touching reds.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Fac: How strongly the change is applied. 0 leaves the image unchanged, 1 is full effect.

CompositorNodeHueSat.node: Shifts the colors, how vivid they are, and their brightness, like the hue and saturation sliders in a photo editor.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Hue: Rotates all colors around the color wheel. 0.5 is no change, away from it shifts reds toward other colors.
inputs.Saturation: Color strength. 0 is black and white, 1 is normal, higher is more vivid.
inputs.Value: Brightness. 0 is black, 1 is normal, higher is brighter.
inputs.Fac: How much of the change is mixed in. 0 shows the original, 1 shows the full adjustment.

CompositorNodeIDMask.node: Turns one object ID from a render into a black and white mask, so you can change just that object.

inputs.ID value: The Object or Material Index pass from the render, where each object has its own number.
inputs.Index: The ID number to pick. Everything with that number turns white, the rest black.
inputs.Anti-Alias: If on, the mask edges are smoothed so they do not look jagged.

CompositorNodeImage.node: Loads a picture, image sequence or video file into the compositor so you can edit it.

CompositorNodeImageCoordinates.node: Outputs the position of each pixel in the image, as a map. Handy for making gradients or warping effects.

inputs.Image: The image whose size is used to work out pixel positions.

CompositorNodeImageInfo.node: Reports facts about an image, such as its width, height and brightness range, as numbers you can use elsewhere.

inputs.Image: The image to read information from.

CompositorNodeInpaint.node: Fills in transparent or missing spots by stretching in nearby colors, like patching a hole with surrounding pixels.

inputs.Image: The picture with holes (transparent areas) to fill.
inputs.Size: How far, in pixels, to grab colors from to fill holes. Low fills only tiny gaps, high fills bigger ones.

CompositorNodeInvert.node: Flips colors to their opposites, like a photo negative, and can also flip transparency.

inputs.Fac: How much to flip. 0 leaves it unchanged, 1 is a full negative, 0.5 turns it flat gray.
inputs.Invert Color: If on, the colors are flipped to their opposites.
inputs.Invert Alpha: If on, the transparency is flipped too: see-through becomes solid and solid becomes see-through.

CompositorNodeKeying.node: An all-in-one green screen remover with cleaning steps: it cuts out the background, tidies the edge and removes color spill.

inputs.Image: The footage with a colored backdrop.
inputs.Key Color: The backdrop color to remove, such as screen green.
inputs.Preprocess Blur Size: Blurs the picture slightly before keying to reduce noise. 0 is none, higher smooths more.
inputs.Key Balance: Balance between the other two colors when finding the key. 0 favors one, 1 favors the other, 0.5 is even.
inputs.Black Level: Values below this become fully transparent in the mask. Raise it to remove more background.
inputs.White Level: Values above this become fully solid in the mask. Lower it to keep more of the subject.
inputs.Edge Search Size: How far from the edge to search when cleaning it, in pixels. Larger looks farther.
inputs.Edge Tolerance: How similar colors must be near the edge to count as the same. Higher treats more as matching.
inputs.Garbage Matte: A mask of areas to always remove, such as lights or stands outside the screen. White areas are cut away.
inputs.Core Matte: A mask of areas to always keep, such as the subject's solid body. White areas stay solid.
inputs.Postprocess Blur Size: Blurs the final mask edge. 0 is none, higher gives a softer edge.
inputs.Postprocess Dilate Size: Grows (positive) or shrinks (negative) the final mask. Use it to trim leftover edge halos.
inputs.Postprocess Feather Size: Makes the mask edge softer by growing or shrinking it with a gradient. Higher gives a wider fade.
inputs.Feather Falloff: The shape of the edge fade, such as Smooth, Sphere or Sharp.
inputs.Despill Strength: How much leftover screen color is removed from the subject. 0 is none, 1 is full cleanup.
inputs.Despill Balance: Balance between the other two colors when removing spill. 0.5 is even.

CompositorNodeKeyingScreen.node: Makes a smooth color backdrop from tracking markers on a green screen, helping the Keying node remove uneven screens.

inputs.Smoothness: How smoothly colors blend between tracked points. Low follows every marker closely, high gives a gentler blend.

CompositorNodeKuwahara.node: Turns an image into a painting-like look by smoothing areas while keeping edges, like an oil painting filter.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Size: Size of the brush strokes. Low keeps detail, high gives big, flat paint patches.
inputs.Type: Classic is faster and simpler, Anisotropic follows the direction of edges for a more natural painted look.
inputs.Uniformity: How evenly the strokes are shaped in Anisotropic mode. Higher makes stroke directions more consistent.
inputs.Sharpness: How crisp the borders between paint patches are. Low is soft, high is sharp.
inputs.Eccentricity: How stretched the brush strokes are along edges. 0 is round, higher is long strokes.
inputs.High Precision: If on, uses a more accurate but slower calculation in Classic mode for smoother results.

CompositorNodeLensdist.node: Bends an image like a camera lens does, or splits colors at the edges. Adds a realistic, imperfect camera look.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Type: Projector gives a simple fixed distortion, Screen Distortion lets you choose the amount and color spreading.
inputs.Distortion: Bends straight lines. Negative bulges outward like a pincushion, positive pinches like a barrel.
inputs.Dispersion: Splits red and blue apart toward the edges, like a cheap lens. 0 is none, higher is more rainbow edges.
inputs.Jitter: If on, adds a little randomness to reduce banding in the color split. Faster but a bit noisy.
inputs.Fit: If on, scales the image so no empty edges show after the distortion.

CompositorNodeLevels.node: Measures the brightness of an image and reports its average and spread as numbers. Handy for automatic adjustments.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Channel: Which part to measure: Combined, Red, Green, Blue or Luminance (brightness).

CompositorNodeLumaMatte.node: Makes pixels transparent based on how bright they are. Use it to cut out very bright or very dark areas.

inputs.Image: The picture to cut by brightness.
inputs.Minimum: Brightness below this becomes fully transparent. Raise it to remove more of the dark parts.
inputs.Maximum: Brightness above this stays fully solid. The space between Minimum and Maximum fades smoothly.

CompositorNodeMapUV.node: Wraps an image onto surfaces using UV coordinates from a render, so you can change a texture after rendering.

inputs.Image: The texture picture to wrap on.
inputs.UV: The UV render pass that tells where each pixel of the texture goes.
inputs.Interpolation: How pixels are blended when moved or resampled. Nearest is crisp and blocky, Bilinear and Bicubic are smoother.
inputs.Extension X: What fills space past the left and right edges. Clip leaves it empty, Extend stretches the edge pixels, Repeat tiles the image.
inputs.Extension Y: What fills space past the top and bottom edges. Clip leaves it empty, Extend stretches the edge pixels, Repeat tiles the image.

CompositorNodeMask.node: Outputs a hand-drawn mask from the Mask Editor as a black and white image, for cutting out or hiding shapes.

inputs.Size Source: Where the mask size comes from: the scene render size or a size you type in.
inputs.Size X: Width of the mask in pixels when using a fixed size.
inputs.Size Y: Height of the mask in pixels when using a fixed size.
inputs.Feather: If on, the soft edges set on the mask shape are used. Off gives hard edges.
inputs.Motion Blur: If on, the mask is smeared by its movement, matching moving footage.
inputs.Motion Blur Samples: How many in-between positions are blended. Low is choppy, high is smooth but slower.
inputs.Motion Blur Shutter: How long the virtual shutter stays open. Low gives light smear, high gives a longer smear.

CompositorNodeMaskToSDF.node: Turns a mask into a map of distances from its edge, which makes it easy to grow, shrink or soften the shape.

inputs.Mask: The black and white mask to measure distances from.

CompositorNodeMovieClip.node: Loads a movie clip you opened in Blender into the compositor, to use with tracking tools or as footage.

CompositorNodeMovieDistortion.node: Adds or removes the lens warp measured from a tracked clip, so graphics and footage match each other.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Type: Undistort removes the lens bend from footage. Distort adds the same bend to a clean image.

CompositorNodeNormal.node: Turns a direction you set with a sphere widget into a vector, and checks how well each normal map pixel lines up with it.

CompositorNodeNormalize.node: Rescales numbers so the lowest becomes 0 and the highest becomes 1. Use it to make a depth map easy to see.

inputs.Value: The gray image or numbers to stretch to fit between 0 and 1.

CompositorNodeOutputFile.node: Saves the image to a file on your computer when you render. You can save several images at once.

CompositorNodePixelate.node: Makes an image blocky, like a low-resolution retro game, by turning small squares into one color.

inputs.Size: Width of each block in pixels. 1 changes nothing, higher makes bigger blocks.

CompositorNodePlaneTrackDeform.node: Sticks an image onto a flat area tracked in a video, like replacing a screen or sign that moves.

inputs.Image: The picture to stick on the tracked area.
inputs.Motion Blur: If on, adds motion blur based on how the plane moves.
inputs.Motion Blur Samples: How many in-between positions are blended. Low is choppy, high is smooth but slower.
inputs.Motion Blur Shutter: How long the virtual shutter stays open. Low gives light blur, high gives strong blur.

CompositorNodePosterize.node: Reduces the number of color levels, so smooth gradients become flat bands, like a screen-printed poster.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Steps: How many levels each color keeps. Low gives a bold, flat look, high looks close to normal.

CompositorNodePremulKey.node: Switches an image between straight and premultiplied alpha, two ways of storing transparency. Fixes dark or bright edge halos.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Type: Chooses the direction: Straight to Premultiplied, or Premultiplied to Straight.

CompositorNodeRGB.node: Outputs a single color you pick. Use it as a flat color source for mixing or backgrounds.

CompositorNodeRGBToBW.node: Turns a color image into black and white, using brightness as seen by the eye.

inputs.Image: The color picture to turn into gray tones.

CompositorNodeRLayers.node: Brings in the render result from your scene, with all its passes like color, depth and normals, ready to edit.

CompositorNodeRelativeToPixel.node: Converts a position or size given as part of the image (0 to 1) into real pixel numbers.

inputs.Vector Value: A 2D value as a fraction of the image. 0.5 means half the width or height.
inputs.Float Value: A single value as a fraction of the image size. 0.5 means half.
inputs.Image: The image whose pixel size is used to convert the value.

CompositorNodeRotate.node: Turns an image around its center by an angle, like spinning a photo on a table.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Angle: How far to turn, in degrees. Positive turns one way, negative turns the other.
inputs.Interpolation: How pixels are blended when moved or resampled. Nearest is crisp and blocky, Bilinear and Bicubic are smoother.
inputs.Extension X: What fills space past the left and right edges. Clip leaves it empty, Extend stretches the edge pixels, Repeat tiles the image.
inputs.Extension Y: What fills space past the top and bottom edges. Clip leaves it empty, Extend stretches the edge pixels, Repeat tiles the image.

CompositorNodeScale.node: Makes an image bigger or smaller, or fits it to the frame size.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Type: How size is set: Relative (by percent), Absolute (pixels), Scene Size (fit render size) or Render Size.
inputs.X: Horizontal size. In Relative mode 1 is the original width, 2 is twice as wide.
inputs.Y: Vertical size. In Relative mode 1 is the original height, 2 is twice as tall.
inputs.Frame Type: For scene-size scaling: Fit keeps all of the image, Crop fills the frame and cuts the overflow, Stretch fills by distorting.
inputs.Interpolation: How pixels are blended when moved or resampled. Nearest is crisp and blocky, Bilinear and Bicubic are smoother.
inputs.Extension X: What fills space past the left and right edges. Clip leaves it empty, Extend stretches the edge pixels, Repeat tiles the image.
inputs.Extension Y: What fills space past the top and bottom edges. Clip leaves it empty, Extend stretches the edge pixels, Repeat tiles the image.

CompositorNodeSceneTime.node: Gives the current time of your animation, as a frame number and in seconds. Use it to animate other nodes.

CompositorNodeSeparateColor.node: Splits a color image into its parts, such as red, green, blue and alpha, so you can edit each one on its own.

inputs.Image: The color picture to split into separate channels.

CompositorNodeSequencerStripInfo.node: Reports information about the video strip being edited, such as its position and length, for use in compositing.

CompositorNodeSetAlpha.node: Replaces or adds the transparency of an image, using a gray map or a number.

inputs.Image: The picture to change the transparency of.
inputs.Alpha: The new transparency. 0 is invisible, 1 is solid. Connect a gray map for changing opacity per pixel.
inputs.Type: Apply Mask multiplies old and new transparency. Replace Alpha throws away the old one.

CompositorNodeSplit.node: Shows two images side by side, split by a line, for comparing before and after.

inputs.Position: Where the dividing line sits, 0 to 1 across the image. 0.5 is the middle.
inputs.Rotation: Turns the dividing line in degrees. 0 is a vertical split, 90 is horizontal.
inputs.Image: The picture shown on the first side of the split.
inputs.Image_001: The picture shown on the other side of the split.

CompositorNodeStabilize.node: Removes camera shake from footage using tracked motion, so the image holds steady.

inputs.Image: The shaky footage to steady.
inputs.Frame: The frame number to read stabilization from. Usually the current frame.
inputs.Invert: If on, puts the shake back in, so you can apply the same camera motion to other graphics.
inputs.Interpolation: How pixels are blended when moved or resampled. Nearest is crisp and blocky, Bilinear and Bicubic are smoother.
inputs.Extension X: What fills space past the left and right edges. Clip leaves it empty, Extend stretches the edge pixels, Repeat tiles the image.
inputs.Extension Y: What fills space past the top and bottom edges. Clip leaves it empty, Extend stretches the edge pixels, Repeat tiles the image.

CompositorNodeStringToImage.node: Turns typed text into an image, so you can put words, labels or titles into your picture.

inputs.Font: The font file or style used for the text.
inputs.Size: How big the letters are. Low is small, high is big.
inputs.Horizontal Alignment: Lines the text left, center or right inside its box.
inputs.Vertical Alignment: Lines the text to the top, middle or bottom inside its box.
inputs.Wrap: If on, long text breaks onto new lines when it reaches the Width.
inputs.Wrap Width: Width in pixels where a line breaks. Smaller gives narrower lines.

CompositorNodeSwitch.node: Picks between two inputs with a checkbox, Use it to turn an effect on and off.

inputs.Switch: If on, the On input is passed through. If off, the Off input is used.
inputs.Off: The image or value used when the switch is off.
inputs.On: The image or value used when the switch is on.

CompositorNodeSwitchView.node: Picks the left or right eye image for 3D stereo renders, so you can edit each eye on its own.

inputs.left: The picture for the left eye of a 3D stereo view.
inputs.right: The picture for the right eye of a 3D stereo view.

CompositorNodeTime.node: Makes a value that changes over time using a curve you draw, like a custom animation timer.

inputs.Start Frame: The frame where the curve starts. Before this the value stays at the curve's beginning.
inputs.End Frame: The frame where the curve ends. After this the value stays at the curve's end.

CompositorNodeTonemap.node: Squeezes a very bright (HDR) image into a range screens can show, keeping detail in lights and darks.

inputs.Image: The HDR picture to compress into a normal brightness range.
inputs.Type: The method: R/D Photoreceptor (mimics eyes) or Rh Simple (a simple formula).
inputs.Key: The overall brightness target. Low makes a darker image, high makes it brighter.
inputs.Balance: Controls the contrast. Low gives a brighter image with softer lights, high gives darker contrast.
inputs.Gamma: Adjusts the mid-tones. Below 1 brightens them, above 1 darkens them.
inputs.Intensity: Overall lightness of the result. Negative darkens, positive brightens.
inputs.Contrast: Difference between lights and darks. Low is flatter, high is more dramatic.
inputs.Light Adaptation: How much each pixel adapts to its own light versus the whole image. 0 is overall, 1 is per pixel.
inputs.Chromatic Adaptation: How much colors adapt to the lighting. 0 keeps the original colors, 1 makes them more neutral.

CompositorNodeTrackPos.node: Reads the position of a tracked point in a video clip as numbers, so you can attach other things to it.

inputs.Mode: How the position is given: Absolute, Relative to the first frame, Relative to a chosen frame, or the position at a frame.
inputs.Frame: The frame number to compare against when the mode is relative to a frame or reads a certain frame.

CompositorNodeTransform.node: Moves, turns and resizes an image in one step. A simple combo of Translate, Rotate and Scale.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.X: Moves the image sideways in pixels. Positive goes right, negative goes left.
inputs.Y: Moves the image up or down in pixels. Positive goes up, negative goes down.
inputs.Angle: Turns the image in degrees around its center.
inputs.Scale: Size multiplier. 1 is original, 2 is twice as big, 0.5 is half.
inputs.Interpolation: How pixels are blended when moved or resampled. Nearest is crisp and blocky, Bilinear and Bicubic are smoother.
inputs.Extension X: What fills space past the left and right edges. Clip leaves it empty, Extend stretches the edge pixels, Repeat tiles the image.
inputs.Extension Y: What fills space past the top and bottom edges. Clip leaves it empty, Extend stretches the edge pixels, Repeat tiles the image.

CompositorNodeTranslate.node: Slides an image sideways or up and down, like moving a photo across a table.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.X: Moves the image sideways in pixels. Positive goes right, negative goes left.
inputs.Y: Moves the image up or down in pixels. Positive goes up, negative goes down.
inputs.Interpolation: How pixels are blended when moved or resampled. Nearest is crisp and blocky, Bilinear and Bicubic are smoother.
inputs.Extension X: What fills space past the left and right edges. Clip leaves it empty, Extend stretches the edge pixels, Repeat tiles the image.
inputs.Extension Y: What fills space past the top and bottom edges. Clip leaves it empty, Extend stretches the edge pixels, Repeat tiles the image.

CompositorNodeVecBlur.node: Adds motion blur to a render using a speed pass, so fast moving things get smeared like in a real camera.

inputs.Image: The picture this node works on. Connect a render, a photo or another node's output here.
inputs.Speed: The Vector pass that says how fast and which way each pixel moves.
inputs.Z: A depth map, used so near objects do not smear over things farther away.
inputs.Samples: How many in-between positions are blended. Low is grainy and fast, high is smooth and slower.
inputs.Shutter: How long the camera shutter stays open. Low gives light blur, high gives long streaks.

CompositorNodeViewer.node: Shows the image at this point in the node tree inside the Backdrop or Image Editor, so you can check your work. It saves nothing.

inputs.Image: The picture to show in the viewer.

CompositorNodeZcombine.node: Combines two images by depth, so whichever is closer to the camera appears in front.

inputs.Depth A: How far each pixel of the first picture is from the camera. Smaller is closer.
inputs.Depth B: How far each pixel of the second picture is from the camera. Smaller is closer.
inputs.Use Alpha: If on, transparent parts of the front picture let the one behind show through.
inputs.Anti-Alias: If on, smooths the jagged edges where one picture overlaps the other.
